Note::permute¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::permute(pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t> dims) const

dims accepts a braced list {1, 0}, a std::vector<std::int64_t>, a std::array, or a std::span.

Reorder All Axes At Once¶

permute() returns a Note whose axes are the input’s axes in the order dims names: dims[i] is the input axis that becomes output axis i. For a 2 × 3 grid, permute({1, 0}) produces the 3 × 2 transpose; for a rank-3 Note, permute({2, 0, 1}) is a full axis rotation that a single transpose cannot express.

Unlike reshape, permute moves cells: the offset table is rebuilt so that reading the result in row-major order visits the cells in their new arrangement. The cell strings themselves are still shared with the source — no text is copied or re-encoded, and the bytes-vs-UTF-8 mode carries over — so the cost is one O(numel) pass over the offset table.

The dims contract¶

dims must be a complete permutation of 0 .. rank-1:

  • its length must equal dim() — otherwise permute expects dims.size() == dim;

  • every value must be in [0, rank) and appear exactly once — otherwise permute dims must be a permutation.

There is no negative-axis form and no partial permutation; name every axis. On a 0-D or 1-D Note the only valid call is permute({}) or permute({0}), both of which return the Note unchanged.

Example 1: The 2-D Transpose¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.permute({1, 0})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3, 2], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "d"], 
  ["b", "e"], 
  ["c", "f"]
]

Output axis 0 is input axis 1 (the old columns), output axis 1 is input axis 0 (the old rows).

Example 2: The Identity Permutation¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.permute({0, 1})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "c"], 
  ["d", "e", "f"]
]

Example 3: A Rank-3 Rotation¶

const auto t = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"}).reshape({1, 2, 3});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(t.permute({2, 0, 1})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3, 1, 2], dim=3, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  [
    ["a", "d"]
  ], 
  [
    ["b", "e"]
  ], 
  [
    ["c", "f"]
  ]
]

The 1 × 2 × 3 shape becomes 3 × 1 × 2: old axis 2 (size 3) moves to the front, old axes 0 and 1 follow.

Example 4: Rejections¶

auto first_line = [](const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string m = e.what();
  return m.substr(0, m.find('\n'));
};

try { (void)pluss::make_note({{"a", "b"}, {"c", "d"}}).permute({0, 0}); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

try { (void)pluss::make_note({{"a", "b"}, {"c", "d"}}).permute({0}); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

Output¶

permute dims must be a permutation
permute expects dims.size() == dim

See Also¶

  • Note::transpose: swap just two axes — the common case, with a shorter call.

  • Note::reshape: regroup the same cells without reordering them.
